text:
katie: Heads up — saw a 3x latency spike on /v1/generate for a customer cohort right after flipping flag `enable_fast_path`. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/internal/dashboards/flag-impact :eyes:

katie: It looks like requests were routed to a fallback model and our quota bump logic didn’t kick in. Repro notes below.

katie: log snippet:
```
2026-03-20T15:01:02Z [route] route=/v1/generate cohort=42 flag=enable_fast_path=true -> fallback_model
2026-03-20T15:01:05Z [quota] predicted_burst=9800 tokens/min, applied=0
2026-03-20T15:01:07Z [latency] p95=820ms p99=1.9s
```

devops-bot: Alert: routing-fallback-rate exceeded 2k/min @ 2026-03-20T15:02Z :rotating_light:

rahul: Was this toggled via console or API? If console, did the UI set a `grace_window` or `staged_rollout`? Sounds like an overwrite.

katie: Console toggle by morgan — they used the quick-edit and it applied at full scope. I think the quick-edit does a replace rather than a merge.

morgan: I did a quick toggle, meant to stage it. The UI flow is confusing — it shows "apply" without clear scope confirmation. Happy to own a modal confirm. Sorry about the blast.

rahul: Two things: 1) We should enforce safer default semantics in the API: PATCH -> merge/patch semantics, PUT -> replace. Right now backend treats both as replace because of our config store wrapper. 2) Add a `dry_run=true` option on writes that lets console show estimated impact (predicted route spillover, quota delta, surge_score).

morgan: +1. UX idea: when scope > 10% show an explicit "staged rollout recommended" and an estimated token delta and predicted fallback risk.

katie: For rollout strategy propose: 0 -> 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 30m observation windows and automated pause if `fallback_rate` or `queue_depth` exceed thresholds. We need preflight checks before the first step.

rahul: Example API snippets (proposal):
````
# merge/patch semantics (safe)
curl -X PATCH "https://api.redwood/configs/enable_fast_path" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -d '{"patch": [{"op":"add","path":"/scope","value":{"cohort_pct":1}}], "dry_run": true}'

# replace (explicit)
curl -X PUT "https://api.redwood/configs/enable_fast_path" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -d '{"scope": {"cohort_pct":100}}'
````

morgan: Good clear separation. Also suggest we store `override_source` meta (console|api|rfc|automation) so dashboard can filter accidental console blasts.

katie: Telemetry: we need per-flag `surge_score` (prediction of risk), per-route `fallback_rate`, and an `override_source` column in the flag timeline panel. I'll add a dashboard card.

morgan: I'll write a short RFC for the API change (split PATCH/PUT semantics, add dry_run). Will also add a console modal confirm for >10% scope toggles.

rahul: I'll prototype a preflight microservice that returns a small risk report used by `dry_run` and the console. It will check historical route latency, current quota headroom, and recent fallback incidents.

katie: I'll add the alert watch and update the runbook playbook with "console quick-edit hazards".

morgan: Action items: (1) morgan RFC + console modal, (2) rahul preflight/dry_run API work, (3) katie dashboard + alert update, (4) ops retro and a short postmortem note.

katie: Sounds good. Owning ops retro.

rahul: I'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to align APIs and preflight schema.

morgan: Sorry again folks, will be more careful. :slightly_smiling_face:

katie: No worries — good catch and quick reactions. :thumbsup:
